issues.display_title: Issue #696: Analytics: integrate Countly Web SDK (countly-sdk-web) reporting to https://data.gothru.org
issues.main_description_html:
Wire the Countly Web SDK into the frontend so sessions, page views, and JS errors are reported to the self-hosted Countly server at https://data.gothru.org.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Current state — what the repo does and does not have

Fact Where
No analytics of any kind today grep for countly/gtag/posthog/mixpanel is empty
The one global client mount point src/app/providers.tsx ("use client", wraps every route from src/app/layout.tsx)
CSP connect-src is a strict allow-list next.config.ts — 'self' + maplibre / openfreemap / gothru.co / arcgis, plus collabCsp derived at build time from NEXT_PUBLIC_COLLAB_URL
Public env var convention NEXT_PUBLIC_*, documented in .env.example, real values in untracked .env.local

The CSP is the part that will silently break this. Every Countly request goes out as XMLHttpRequest (node_modules/countly-sdk-web/lib/countly.js:6721) — there is no image beacon and no injected <script> on the paths we use, so adding the Countly origin to connect-src is both necessary and sufficient. The createElement("iframe") / createElement("script") paths inside the SDK belong to the feedback-widget and boomerang APM plugins, which this task does not enable — so frame-src, script-src, and img-src stay untouched.

Scope

  1. Dependency — countly-sdk-web (26.1.3). Ships its own lib/countly.d.ts, no @types package needed.
  2. src/lib/analytics/countly.ts — a lazy singleton that import()s the SDK on first use, calls Countly.init({ app_key, url }) exactly once, and turns on track_sessions() + track_errors(). Returns null when there is no app key or no window, so every call site degrades to a no-op.
  3. src/components/analytics/CountlyAnalytics.tsx — "use client", renders null, reports track_pageview(pathname) on every App Router navigation via usePathname().
  4. Mount — inside Providers so it covers every route, including /embed and the public /v/[key] viewer.
  5. CSP — derive the Countly origin from NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_URL in next.config.ts the same way collabCsp is derived, and append it to connect-src.
  6. .env.example — document NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_APP_KEY.
  7. Test — src/lib/analytics/__tests__/countly.test.ts: no app key ⇒ no SDK load and no init; app key ⇒ init called once across repeated calls.

Decisions made on purpose

  • Dynamic import() inside an effect, not a static import. The SDK touches window/localStorage; a static import puts it in the server bundle and in the initial client chunk for a payload nobody needs before hydration.
  • No app key ⇒ the SDK is never even downloaded. That is the dev/CI default, so no local session ever pollutes production data.
  • usePathname() only, not useSearchParams(). useSearchParams forces a Suspense boundary or a full client-render bailout on every page that mounts it — too high a price for query strings in a view name. Countly still records the full URL itself.
  • No consent gating (require_consent) for now. Add it when the cookie/consent banner exists; wiring an always-granted consent call today is dead code.
  • The app key is not committed. It goes in .env.local on dev and in /home/config on the prod host.

Acceptance criteria

  • With NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_APP_KEY set, loading any page produces begin_session + a view request to https://data.gothru.org/i with HTTP 200, and no CSP violation in the console.
  • Client-side navigation (e.g. dashboard → editor) reports a new view without a full page load.
  • With the app key unset, countly-sdk-web is never fetched and nothing is logged or thrown.
  • No window is not defined during pnpm build / SSR.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit all green.

RESULT

Countly Web SDK is wired in and merged to development and main.

File What it does
src/lib/analytics/countly.ts Memoised lazy loader. Dynamic import("countly-sdk-web") on first use, one init({ app_key, url, debug }), then track_sessions() + track_errors(). Resolves to null — never rejects — when there is no app key or no window, so a blocked chunk or an unreachable Countly cannot surface as an unhandled rejection.
src/components/analytics/CountlyAnalytics.tsx "use client", renders null, calls track_pageview(pathname) on every App Router navigation via usePathname().
src/app/providers.tsx Mounts it inside ThemeProvider, so it covers every route — there is exactly one root layout, so /embed and the public /v/[key] viewer are included.
next.config.ts countlyCsp derives the origin from NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_URL (same shape as collabCsp) and appends it to connect-src, in both the 'self' and the /v/:path+ * header branches, since both go through the same securityHeaders().
.env.example Documents NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_APP_KEY.
src/lib/analytics/__tests__/countly.test.ts 3 cases, jsdom: no app key ⇒ SDK never loaded and init never called; repeated calls ⇒ one init, one track_sessions, one track_errors, same instance; explicit NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_URL is honoured.

countly-sdk-web@26.1.3 ships its own lib/countly.d.ts, so no @types package was needed.

Server check: POST https://data.gothru.org/i?app_key=ping&... answers {"result":"App does not exist"} — the ingest endpoint is live and reachable, it just has no app registered for that key yet.

Verification: pnpm test 1220 passed / 3 skipped (148 files), pnpm lint clean, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Still needed before any data appears: create the application in the Countly dashboard at https://data.gothru.org, then set NEXT_PUBLIC_COUNTLY_APP_KEY — in .env.local for dev and in /home/config on the prod host. Both NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars are inlined at build time, so the frontend has to be rebuilt, not just restarted, for the key and the CSP origin to take effect.

Commits: 6241c0d (feature), 0d14e4f (merge → development), a5b96f6 (merge → main).
Branch: feature/696-countly-web-sdk.

issues.display_title: Issue #697: fix(analytics): stop sending public share keys to Countly, and double-reporting views under StrictMode
issues.main_description_html:
Two defects in the Countly view reporting shipped by #696, both in the same file. Neither is hypothetical: the app key is now set, so both are affecting live data.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

1. The public share key is being sent to Countly

src/components/analytics/CountlyAnalytics.tsx:20 reports track_pageview(pathname), and on the public viewer the pathname is the share key — /v/ab12cd34. That key is the access credential for a customer's published indoor map (src/lib/preview/publish.ts:25); anyone who can open the Countly dashboard can read a list of every published map and open them. /embed/[key] has the same shape, and /editor/[projectId] and /preview/[projectId] leak project UUIDs.

It is also a data-quality problem on its own: Countly writes one app_viewsmeta document per distinct view name, so the Views report becomes an unbounded list of one-hit keys and the aggregate question — how many editor sessions, how many public-viewer opens — cannot be read off the dashboard at all. /v and /embed are the highest-traffic routes, so they dominate the noise.

Note that the SDK stamps a second field, view, from Countly.getViewUrl() (node_modules/countly-sdk-web/lib/countly.js:7913), which returns window.location.pathname — so passing a normalised name to track_pageview is not enough on its own. getViewUrl is an overridable namespace function (countly.d.ts:576); override it too, or the raw key still leaves the browser on every view.

Fix: normalise dynamic segments before reporting, and override getViewUrl to the same normalised value.

Route Reported as
/v/<key> /v/[key]
/embed/<key> /embed/[key]
/editor/<uuid> /editor/[projectId]
/preview/<uuid> /preview/[projectId]

2. StrictMode reports every dev page view twice

src/components/analytics/CountlyAnalytics.tsx:19 has no double-invoke guard. next.config.ts sets no reactStrictMode, and Next defaults __NEXT_STRICT_MODE_APP to true, so the dev server mounts → unmounts → remounts the component and the effect body runs twice for the same pathname. The memoised promise in countly() dedupes init(), not the .then callbacks.

Reproduced against the real SDK: two back-to-back track_pageview("/editor/abc") calls queue [CLY]_view {visit:1, start:1}, then a spurious [CLY]_view {dur:0} closing it after zero seconds, then a second {visit:1} with a fresh view id. Root cause is in the SDK — track_pageview calls reportViewDuration() unconditionally (countly.js:3956) and has no same-name dedupe.

Dev-only (StrictMode double-invokes effects only in React dev builds), but .env.local now carries a real app key pointing at the same Countly app as production, so every dev page load adds 2 visits and drags the average view duration toward 0.

Fix: guard on the last reported view name with a ref — refs survive StrictMode's simulated remount, and a real navigation still reports because the value differs.

Acceptance criteria

  • A page load in pnpm dev produces exactly one [CLY]_view, with no dur:0 closer.
  • Opening a published map reports the view name /v/[key], and the event's view field is /v/[key] too — the raw key appears in neither.
  • Static routes (/, /dashboard, /login) are unchanged.
  • Unit test covers the normaliser table above and the StrictMode double-mount.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Both defects fixed and merged to development via #704.

1. Share key / project id no longer leave the browser. normalizeViewPath() in src/lib/analytics/countly.ts collapses /v/<key> → /v/[key], /embed/<key> → /embed/[key], /editor/<uuid> → /editor/[projectId], /preview/<uuid> → /preview/[projectId]. The pattern is deliberately unanchored at the end, so any deeper path under those prefixes collapses to the same template rather than leaking a segment nobody anticipated.

As the issue predicted, normalising the name passed to track_pageview was not sufficient on its own — the SDK stamps a second URL field from getViewUrl() (countly.js:7913), which returns window.location.pathname verbatim. getViewUrl is now overridden to the same normaliser, and the override is installed before init() so it is in place ahead of the first view.

2. StrictMode double-report fixed. src/components/analytics/CountlyAnalytics.tsx guards on a useRef holding the last reported pathname. The comparison deliberately uses the raw pathname, not the normalised name: comparing the normalised value would have made a real navigation between two projects report only once, since both collapse to /editor/[projectId].

Tests

  • src/lib/analytics/__tests__/countly.test.ts — 9 normaliser cases (4 dynamic routes, a deeper path under /v, and 5 static routes left untouched), plus one asserting sdk.getViewUrl() returns /v/[key] while window.location.pathname is /v/ab12cd34.
  • src/components/analytics/__tests__/CountlyAnalytics.test.tsx — 3 cases rendered inside a real <StrictMode>: one view per mount despite the double invoke, the route template rather than the share key on the public viewer, and two reports when the user moves between two projects.

The tests were checked against a broken implementation, not just run green. With the ref guard removed, all three component tests fail with expected 1 times, but got 2 times — so the StrictMode double-invoke is genuinely reproduced under vitest rather than passing vacuously.

Verification

pnpm test 1234 passed / 3 skipped (149 files) · pnpm lint clean · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Note

.cly-probe.mjs was found untracked in the repo root — a leftover debug script from the review that produced this issue. It was excluded from the commit and moved out of the tree, not committed.

Commits: e6f0bf9 (fix), 9207c75 (merge of #704 into development).
Branch: feature/697-countly-view-privacy.

issues.display_title: Issue #698: Analytics: wizard funnel events + shared trackEvent helper (Countly)
issues.main_description_html:
Instrument the setup wizard funnel with Countly custom events, and add the small shared helper the rest of the analytics work will build on. From the event inventory run against #696.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Why this one first

All four wizard steps render at the same URL (/start), so CountlyAnalytics.tsx fires exactly one view for the entire wizard. The product's most important funnel — how many visitors reach a finished project, and which step they abandon — is currently invisible, and no amount of view tracking will fix it.

Shared helper (lands here, used by every later analytics task)

A thin wrapper over countly() in src/lib/analytics/, so call sites read as one line and the event keys live in one place. Nothing elaborate: a trackEvent(key, { segmentation, count, sum, dur }) that no-ops when the SDK is off, plus the key union type. Server actions cannot call it — the SDK is browser-only — so every event below fires from the client caller, not from src/actions/.

Events

wizard_step_entered

  • Call site: src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts:248, inside the existing useMapStore.subscribe((state, prev) => ...) registered by the effect at :244. It already discriminates step transitions at :251 and :276, so prev is handed to you.
  • Not WizardShell.tsx — and this is load-bearing, not a style call. React runs child effects before parent effects; StartPage (src/app/start/page.tsx:7) calls useWizardPersistence and then renders WizardShell, and the synchronous restoreFromLocal() → hydratePersistedState → setCurrentSetupStep(lastVisited) (src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts:194) runs in the parent's effect. A WizardShell effect always observes step 0 first, so a resumed wizard would be reported as a real 0→2 forward walk and silently inflate the funnel.
  • Guard, required: the same hook is mounted by src/app/editor/[projectId]/page.tsx:17, and wizardState.ts:194 mutates currentSetupStep on every editor open. Without if (projectId) return; every editor load emits phantom wizard steps. The effect at :244 already closes over projectId (used at :235).
  • Segmentation: step: 0_location | 1_floors | 2_order | 3_generate (index-prefixed so Countly's alphabetical value dropdown reads in wizard order) · direction: enter | forward | back (enter from a one-shot mount emit; an enter with step > 0_location is the resume signal) · max_step_reached: 0|1|2|3 from lastVisitedStep (src/store/mapStore/wizardSlice.ts:8).
  • Fire on entry, not as a timed event. start_event/end_event only send on end_event, so the step a user abandons never reports — precisely the one you need.

wizard_location_confirmed

  • Call site: src/components/setup/StepSelectLocation.tsx:138 (handleConfirm) — after the await at :143-153, and in the catch at :154.
  • Segmentation: result: created | reused | failed · coord_mode: pin | manual · address_present: bool.
  • Never send the raw failure text — :155 surfaces err.message straight from the Go API.

floor_plan_upload

  • Call site: src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx:104 (xhr.onload success) and the shared fail helper at :71, which already covers HTTP non-2xx (:90), bad body (:107) and network error (:110). Client-side rejections happen before any request: :263 (unsupported MIME), :267 (over MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB).
  • Segmentation: result: success | http_error | bad_response | network_error | rejected_format | rejected_size | no_project · mime (raw file.type, "unknown" when the browser gives "") · ext (lowercased, derived from the name) · size_mb: <1 | 1-5 | 5-10 | >10 · batch_size: 1 | 2-5 | 6-20 | 20+ · status (only when result=http_error).
  • Worth having because a failed upload leaves the user stuck: Continue stays disabled until every file has a serverPath.

wizard_completed

  • Call site: src/lib/wizard/completeWizard.ts:24, before the localStorage wipe. Four callers funnel through it: StepGenerate.tsx:87 and :95, StepUploadFloor.tsx:184, useWizardPersistence.ts:289.
  • Segmentation: exit: generated | blank_canvas | import · floors (count) · no_project: bool.
  • completeWizard is a plain module but browser-only anyway because of its localStorage write, so countly() is safe there even though the updateProject it calls on :25 is a server action.

project_start_method

  • Call site: src/components/projects/NewProjectFlow.tsx:169 (ChoiceCard variant="scan"); the competing branch is :170 (empty canvas, which creates a project directly at :123-131 and never enters the wizard).
  • Segmentation: method: scan_floor_plan | empty_canvas · source: dashboard | editor_file_menu.

PII rules for this task

Never segment on: location.address, location.lat/lng (wizardSlice.ts:9, rendered at 6 decimal places in StepSelectLocation.tsx:42-43 — that pinpoints a building), projectName (routinely a client's company name), projectId, and anything from uploadedFiles — file.name and the returned serverPath are a customer filename and a raw storage key.

Acceptance criteria

  • Every event above appears in Countly with the exact keys and bounded values listed; no free text, no ids.
  • Walking the wizard end to end produces one wizard_step_entered per transition and exactly one wizard_completed.
  • Opening the editor produces zero wizard events.
  • A resumed wizard reports direction=enter at its restored step, not a forward walk from 0.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

All five events plus the shared helper are in, merged to development via #705.

File What landed
src/lib/analytics/events.ts trackEvent(key, payload) over countly(), with AnalyticsEvent as a union so a typo is a type error. Plus the bucket helpers every later task will reuse: sizeBucketMb, countBucket, fileExtension, wizardStepLabel.
src/lib/analytics/uploadEvent.ts reportUpload() — the upload has six outcomes across three call sites and the segmentation has to be identical at all of them.
src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts wizard_step_entered from the existing store subscriber, plus a one-shot mount emit above it.
src/components/setup/StepSelectLocation.tsx wizard_location_confirmed.
src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx floor_plan_upload, wired through fail() so every failure path is covered by one change.
src/lib/wizard/completeWizard.ts wizard_completed, plus the new WizardExit type; the four callers pass their exit and floor count.
src/components/projects/NewProjectFlow.tsx project_start_method.

Everything the issue asked for was confirmed against the tree

  • The WizardShell ordering hazard is real, and the report lives in the hook's subscriber instead. Covered by a test that pre-sets step 2 before mount and asserts the entry reports 2_order, not a walk from 0.
  • The editor guard is in and tested: mounting the hook with a projectId and then moving currentSetupStep emits nothing.
  • Fires on entry, not as a timed event.
  • source on NewProjectFlow really was dead — declared on Props, passed by both call sites, never destructured. Now used.

Two things the issue did not anticipate

  1. projectId had to join the subscriber effect's dependency array. It was [disabled] and did not reference the prop before; now it does, and react-hooks/exhaustive-deps flagged it. A stale value there is exactly the phantom-editor-steps bug the guard exists to prevent.
  2. wizard_completed needed per-project deduplication. The generate path reaches completeWizard twice — the store subscriber latches the project complete the moment the twin appears (useWizardPersistence.ts), then the user presses Open Editor (StepGenerate.tsx). Without the guard every generated project counted as two finished wizards.

Behaviour note

An upload returning 2xx with no serverPath is now reported as bad_response rather than success. That state leaves the row looking finished while Continue stays disabled. No app behaviour changed — only the reporting is honest about it.

Tests

  • src/lib/analytics/__tests__/events.test.ts — 18 cases: payload shape, count default and override, and every bucket boundary.
  • src/hooks/__tests__/useWizardPersistence.funnel.test.tsx — 4 cases: entry under a real <StrictMode> wrapper, the resumed-step case, forward/back directions, and silence in the editor.
  • src/lib/wizard/__tests__/completeWizard.test.ts — 4 added cases: exit and floor count, the no-project case, the duplicate-completion dedupe, and silence when no analytics argument is passed.

Checked against a broken implementation, not just run green: removing the entry-report ref guard makes the StrictMode test fail with expected [2 items] to deeply equal [1 item].

Privacy

No address, coordinate, project name, floor name, file name, server path, or raw error string is reported. Only bounded labels, buckets, and counts.

Verification

pnpm test 1260 passed / 3 skipped (151 files) · pnpm lint clean with zero warnings · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Commits: 769009f (feature), 186ae94 (merge of #705 into development).
Branch: feature/698-wizard-funnel-events.

issues.display_title: Issue #699: Analytics: AI floor plan scan and import events (Countly)
issues.main_description_html:
Instrument the ingestion paths — AI floor-plan scan, Mappedin import, and virtual-tour lookup. From the event inventory run against #696. Depends on the trackEvent helper landing in the wizard-funnel task.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Why

These are the slow, failure-prone, money-costing paths. The AI scan is the only GPU call the product makes, and today there is no way to answer what its p95 latency is, how often it fails, or why. Each of these events has two call sites — one in the wizard, one in the editor's Add Floor flow — so a surface segment keeps them a single event key instead of two near-duplicates.

Events

floor_plan_scan — one per floor scanned

  • Call sites: src/components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx:141 (wrap predictFloorplanTxt inside generateFloor, which starts at :136, plus the missing-file throw at :139) and src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts:229 (inside scanAddedFloor, :222).
  • In the wizard, catch, fire, then rethrow so src/components/setup/step-generate/machine.ts:76-79 still marks the floor failed. Do not instrument machine.ts itself — it is a pure, unit-tested module and the SDK does not belong in it.
  • Segmentation: surface: wizard_generate | editor_add_floor · outcome: success | no_file | http_error | stream_error | stream_ended · wall_source: net | cv · wall_threshold: default | custom (default is 0.5 at StepGenerate.tsx:56 and useAddLevel.ts:35) · attempt: first | retry_floor | retry_all.
  • outcome needs a real error code first. Today the five throws in src/lib/.../predictClient.ts (:31, :34, :60, :62, :67) carry only a message. Attach a code property to them; never derive the outcome by matching err.message.
  • Duration: add_event({ dur }) from a performance.now() delta. Not start_event/end_event — concurrent floors would clobber the keyed timer.

floor_plan_scan_run — one per Generate press

  • Call site: src/components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx:162 (startGeneration) through :180, after runGeneration at :178 and rebuildTwin() at :179. Same event from retryFailed (:188) and retryFloor (:196).
  • Segmentation: trigger: initial | retry_failed | retry_floor · outcome: all_success | partial | all_failed · floors_total: 1 | 2-3 | 4-6 | 7+ · floors_skipped_imported: 0 | 1+ · wall_source · wall_threshold. Put the floors-scanned count in sum and the elapsed ms in dur.
  • Gotcha: immediately after await runGeneration, the floors state in the closure is stale. Derive the counts from resultsRef (:60), not from floors.

floor_plan_import — Mappedin / MapThru file import

  • Call sites: src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx:123 (runImport(file) in handleFileSelected, :118) and src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts:152.
  • Segmentation: surface: wizard_step2 | editor_add_floor · outcome: ok | unreadable | empty (runImport.ts:25,31,34) · kind: zip | editor (detectSource.ts:22, omitted when outcome ≠ ok) · ext: zip | json | geojson | txt | other (whitelist, already computed at useAddLevel.ts:112-114) · size_bucket: <1MB | 1-10MB | 10-50MB | 50MB+ · floors_bucket, locations_bucket, buildings_bucket. Raw floor count goes in sum, parse ms in dur.

mappedin_import_reviewed — did the review modal convert

  • Call sites: src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx:141 (handleContinueToEditor), :197 (handleAddMoreFloors), dismissal via the modal's onClose at :475; editor equivalent src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts:173 (handleConfirmImport).
  • Segmentation: surface: wizard | editor · action: committed | add_more_floors | dismissed. Levels imported goes in sum.
  • A parse that succeeds is worthless if the user bails at review, which is exactly what this separates.

virtual_tour_load

  • Call site: src/components/editor/add-panorama/AddPanoramaModal.tsx:272 (success) and :276 (failure), around the await processTour(value) at :270. Not :262-264 (empty input) and not the superseded early returns at :271/:274.
  • Segmentation: outcome: loaded | empty_no_map_widget | input_invalid | tour_not_found | overlay_unreachable | unexpected. dur from a Date.now() captured before :270 — again not start_event/end_event, concurrent loads clobber it.
  • This is the slowest third-party fetch in the product: one tour lookup fans out to one JSON per panorama, in serial.

PII rules for this task

  • Never send serverPath — it is minio:///{projectId}/{fileName} (src/app/api/upload/route.ts:62), an internal object key.
  • Never send err.message. StepGenerate.tsx:139 interpolates the user-typed floor name into the Error, and predictClient.ts:29 forwards the Go API's error string verbatim. Bucket into the codes above.
  • Never send anything off a Mappedin export: src.location (StepUploadFloor.tsx:146) carries the customer's real venue name, address and coordinates; location titles and descriptions are customer content.
  • Highest risk in this task: the virtual-tour input is a share key. Never send input/value (AddPanoramaModal.tsx:250), result.tourKey, or pano image/thumbnail URLs — those embed {userId}/{cid}/{tourKey}.

Acceptance criteria

  • A wizard Generate over 3 floors with one failure produces 3 floor_plan_scan and 1 floor_plan_scan_run with outcome=partial.
  • The same scan run from the editor's Add Floor reports surface=editor_add_floor under the same event key.
  • predictClient.ts throws carry a code; no outcome is derived from message text.
  • No share key, filename, serverPath, or venue field appears in any segmentation value.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

All five events are in, merged to development via #706.

Event Wizard call site Editor call site
floor_plan_scan ⏱ StepGenerate.tsx generateFloor useAddLevel.ts scanAddedFloor
floor_plan_scan_run ⏱ runScan(), shared by Generate / Retry Failed / Row Retry —
floor_plan_import ⏱ StepUploadFloor.tsx handleFileSelected useAddLevel.ts handleImport
mappedin_import_reviewed handleContinueToEditor / handleAddMoreFloors / modal onClose handleConfirmImport
virtual_tour_load ⏱ — AddPanoramaModal.tsx process()

New shared modules: src/lib/analytics/scanEvent.ts (reportScan, scanOutcome, runOutcome) and src/lib/analytics/importEvent.ts (reportImport, reportImportReviewed). Both surfaces of each event go through one reporter, so the segmentation cannot drift between them.

The prerequisite, done as specified

predictClient.ts now throws PredictError with a code of http_error, no_stream, stream_error or stream_ended. Anything else reports "unknown"; no outcome is derived from message text. The messages the UI shows are unchanged — only a property was added. predictErrorCode() is the single reader.

Decisions

  • dur rather than start_event/end_event, exactly as the issue asked: a wizard run scans floors back to back and a keyed timer would be clobbered by the next floor. Same reasoning for two Process presses in the panorama modal.
  • Run outcomes are tallied in a ref as each floor settles, not read back off floors — that state is stale in the closure the moment await runGeneration(...) returns.
  • runOutcome(ok, failed) was extracted so the three-way all_success / partial / all_failed branch is covered by a test instead of living inline in a component.

One thing the issue did not anticipate

A run over zero scannable floors reported a vacuous all_success. startGeneration still reaches the reporting path when every floor came from an import and none can be scanned. It now returns before reporting.

Tests

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/__tests__/predictClient.test.ts — 6 cases added to the 2 already there: every failure code, plus predictErrorCode falling back to unknown for a non-PredictError.
  • src/lib/analytics/__tests__/scanImportEvents.test.ts — 14 cases: dur placement, threshold reduced to default/custom, surface and attempt pass-through, classification by code rather than message, the runOutcome truth table, import buckets, the failure path omitting parsed counts, unknown extensions collapsing to other, and one asserting a venue-named file never appears in the payload.

Correction

While writing the tests I overwrote src/lib/floorplanEditor/__tests__/predictClient.test.ts, dropping its two existing cases. issues.main_description_html:
Instrument the editor — which tools get used, whether levels get added, and whether saving is quietly failing. From the event inventory run against #696. Depends on the trackEvent helper landing in the wizard-funnel task.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Events

editor_tool_selected

  • Call sites: src/components/editor/FloorplanEditor.tsx:292 (all 2D tools, toolbar and keyboard alike), the Shapes dropdown at :737, and src/components/editor/EditorBottomToolbar.tsx:42/:43/:94 for the map surface. Fire only when the mode value is non-null.
  • Do not instrument FloorplanEditor.tsx:752 — the access dropdown already emits mode("access") via index.ts:142 and would double-count.
  • Segmentation: tool: wall | curveWall | door | window | area | point | safety | access | shape_rect | shape_circle | shape_polygon | select | drag_building | wall_vertex · surface: floorplan | map · via: toolbar | keyboard.
  • The single biggest unknown in the product: roughly 14 tools ship and nobody knows which are reached for. This is the highest-volume event in the editor, so no ids in segmentation — nanoid level/building values would blow up Countly's cardinality.

floor_plan_save_failed

  • Call site: src/components/editor/EditorTopbar.tsx:122.
  • Segmentation: stage: update_project | save_floorplan | unknown (not derivable from failureMessage — set a stage variable before each await, i.e. before :101 and before :111) · trigger: autosave | unmount_flush | manual (pass as a saveNow(trigger) argument so :151, the timer, is distinguishable from :141, the unmount flush) · reason: unauthorized | forbidden | server | network | unknown.
  • unauthorized is the exact string saveFloorplanAction returns when there is no access token (src/actions/projects.ts:272) and is the most valuable bucket here.
  • Autosave is the product's data-durability promise and its failure is invisible today — the catch writes a message and nothing else. A user can lose an editing session and we would never know.

level_added

  • Call site: src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts:196 — turn it into addFloorOnce(source) firing after the dedupe guard at :197, with "blank" from :218 and "ai_scan" from :247.
  • Segmentation: source: blank | ai_scan | txt_import | txt_drop_empty | mappedin_import · into_existing_building: true | false (from selectedBuildingId != null; omit the key entirely on mappedin_import). Level count goes in count: 1 for the four single-level paths, merged.floorConfigs.length - store.floorConfigs.length for the import.
  • Levels are the unit of work in indoor mapping and there are four completely different ways to get one, which is exactly the split worth seeing.

panorama_import

  • Call site: src/components/editor/floorplan-editor/AddPanoramaButton.tsx:53.
  • Segmentation: outcome: imported | no_panoramas | lookup_failed · error_code: input_invalid | tour_not_found | load_failed (only on lookup_failed, from AddPanoramaModal.tsx:274-276) · alignment_applied: bool (the 4th arg of onImported, currently discarded as _viaAlignment) · had_positions: bool (the canAlign expression already computed at AddPanoramaModal.tsx:55). Panorama count goes in sum.
  • Panorama placement is how a floor plan becomes a walkable digital twin.

PII rules for this task

Never send the floor name (useAddLevel.ts:199 — free user text, and on imports it comes straight out of a customer's file), file.name, serverPath, raw error strings (res.error is server text that can carry ids or paths), tour.tourKey or the pasted tour URL (AddPanoramaModal.tsx:250), or any projectId/levelId.

Explicitly out of scope

No event per save. The editor autosaves 2 seconds after every change; an event there would dwarf everything else in the app. The "how much mapping actually got done" question is answered by a single summary event on leave, which is tracked separately in the phase-2 task.

Acceptance criteria

  • Selecting each tool once, by toolbar and by keyboard, produces one event per selection with the right via, and the access dropdown produces exactly one — not two.
  • Forcing a save failure (revoke the token) produces floor_plan_save_failed with reason=unauthorized and the correct trigger.
  • Adding a level by each of the five sources reports the matching source.
  • No id, filename, or free-text name appears in any segmentation value.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

All four events are in, merged to development via #707. New reporters: src/lib/analytics/toolEvent.ts, saveEvent.ts, levelEvent.ts, panoramaEvent.ts.

Five things in this issue were wrong against the current tree

Stated Actual
the access dropdown emits via index.ts:142 :140. The claim is correct, the line is not — :142 is a comment inside the setShapeTool doc block. Verified chain: index.ts:140 → commands.ts:69 setAddMode → :54 applyAdd → :58 ctx.on.mode(ctx.addKind), all synchronous. FloorplanEditor.tsx:752 is correctly left uninstrumented.
a saveNow(trigger) argument covers all three triggers It cannot. The Save button never goes through saveNow — handleSave calls saveFloorplanAction directly — so manual needed its own two reports. handleSave's signature was deliberately not changed: onClick={handleSave} would pass the React MouseEvent as the first argument.
panorama_import carries lookup_failed, no_panoramas and error_code All three are structurally unreachable. onImported is only called from commit(), which bails unless the modal state is loaded, and the Import buttons only render when panoramas.length > 0. The lookup is already covered end to end by virtual_tour_load (#699). Keeping them would have double-reported the same thing under two keys.
_viaAlignment is the 4th arg and is discarded It is the 3rd; the 4th, positions, is used.
line numbers in useAddLevel.ts and AddPanoramaModal.tsx All shifted by #699.

What the events ended up as

  • editor_tool_selected — tool (14 closed values) · surface (editor_2d / map) · source (toolbar / keyboard). Reported from the engine's mode callback for the 8 engine tools, directly from the Shapes dropdown for the 3 shapes, and from the three map handlers.
  • floor_plan_save_failed — stage · trigger · reason · status · role. Three report sites: the saveNow catch, and both failure exits of handleSave.
  • level_added — source (5 values) · into_existing_building (omitted for imports) · Countly count (36 for a 36-floor import, not 36 events).
  • panorama_import — outcome (imported / no_level / no_canvas) · alignment_applied · any_aligned · had_positions · dropped · count_bucket (conditional) · sum = panoramas placed.

What made the naive edit wrong

  1. The mode callback fires with null constantly — every mount, floor switch, file load and remote collab apply, plus Escape and the deselect re-click. toolForMode returns undefined for anything unmapped and the report is skipped; otherwise null would be the highest-volume value in the event.
  2. Toolbar and keyboard are indistinguishable at that callback — applyAdd has no origin argument. A ref raised immediately before the engine call and reset on every callback entry recovers it, safe only because the callback fires synchronously inside setAddMode. The access dropdown bypasses setAddMode, so it raises the flag without reporting.
  3. Shapes are the mirror image — setShapeTool clears addKind first, so the engine only ever emits mode(null) for them; they report from the dropdown row.
  4. level_added sits inside addFloorOnce, below the dedupe guard. In handleAddAndScanFloor instead, every Retry Scan would count a second level.
  5. caps.role is read through a ref. In saveNow's dependency array it would change the callback's identity when the role resolves, and the unmount-flush effect depends on saveNow — every role resolution would fire an extra save labelled unmount_flush. react-hooks/refs also rejects a ref write during render, so it lives in an effect.
  6. The map toggles report only their ON transition, and Drag is guarded on !mapMoveMode.

Known caveat, deliberately not fixed

The unmount-flush effect has deps [caps.canEdit, saveNow], and canEdit starts false and flips true once the role resolves, so its cleanup runs while the component is still mounted. Pre-existing behaviour, but those saves now carry trigger: unmount_flush — so that value is not perfectly trustworthy. Fixing it changes when saves happen, which is outside this task.

Also noted: EditorBottomToolbar and EditorTopbar are both rendered by src/app/design-preview/collaboration/CollaborationPreview.tsx, which seeds the store for real. Interacting with that internal page emits real events. Low volume, not gated.

Tests

src/lib/analytics/__tests__/editorEvents.test.ts — 21 cases across the four reporters: the full toolForMode mapping and its rejection of null/""/unmapped values, the save reason buckets including offline vs unknown and a missing navigator, the import count and omitted building flag, and the panorama outcome/bucket/alignment logic.

Checked against broken implementations, not just run green. Making toolForMode fall back to "select" and making count_bucket unconditional (countBucket(0) returns "1", so a zero-placement import would report as a batch of one) each fail the suite; both were reverted.

Privacy

No id, file name, floor name, venue name, tour key, coordinate, email address or raw error string is reported. Three tests assert specifically that the owner email, the tour key and a venue-named file never reach a payload.

Instrument the project lifecycle and the public viewer — publish, share, and what end customers actually do on a published indoor map. From the event inventory run against #696. Depends on the trackEvent helper landing in the wizard-funnel task.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Why

This is the only group of events that proves the product delivers value to anyone other than the person building the map. Everything upstream measures effort; these measure whether the result gets opened, searched, and navigated.

Events

indoor_map_opened

  • Call site: src/app/v/[key]/page.tsx:41 (setStatus("ready") after hydratePersistedState) and :37 (the error branch behind "This project is not available." at :55).
  • Segmentation: outcome: available | unavailable · surface: live | embed · framing: standalone | iframe_tour | iframe_other · levels: 1 | 2-3 | 4-9 | 10+ (success rows only).
  • No project id, no share key, no location.

project_publish

  • Call sites: src/app/dashboard/useDashboard.ts:168-170 (handlePublishToggle) and src/components/preview/PreviewTopbar.tsx:100/:119 (confirmPublish/confirmUnpublish). These are the only two callers in src/; the server actions at src/actions/projects.ts:189/:202 cannot fire the event themselves.

project_shared

  • Call site: src/components/preview/PreviewShareModal.tsx:14 — the single useCopy handler all three sections route through (LinkSection :127, EmbedSection :166, EmbedTourSection :231).
  • Segmentation: channel: share_link | tour_embed | website_embed · result: copied | error (the error branch is real — blocked clipboard or insecure context, clipboard.ts:13/:18) · surface: preview_navbar | dashboard_menu.
  • surface needs a new required prop on PreviewShareModal, passed as a literal from PreviewTopbar.tsx:297 and ProjectViews.tsx:234. That is not free — it breaks the 3-prop render in renameSweep.test.ts:63, so update that test in the same change.

project_created

  • Call site: src/components/projects/NewProjectFlow.tsx:123, after createProject resolves and before the router.push at :131.
  • Segmentation: workflow: scan | empty_canvas | mappedin_import · entry_source: dashboard | editor_file_menu | wizard · location_source: address | map | coordinates | default (map the null at :29 to the literal "default", do not send null) · has_address: bool · result: ok | error.

map_object_selected

  • Call sites: src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx:676 (marker/label select), :502 (label-canvas click) and :600 (handleSearchSelect).
  • Segmentation: via: map | marker | search · kind: area | point | safety | access | shape (Selection.kind, previewPinUtils.ts:5) · surface: editor | preview | live | embed — four values, not three: editor is the bare <PreviewOverlay /> at app/editor/[projectId]/page.tsx:66, preview is app/preview/[projectId]/page.tsx:52, live/embed both come from app/v/[key]/page.tsx:60.

directions_route_planned

  • Call site: a useEffect keyed on [routeKey (PreviewOverlay.tsx:363), routeStatus (:213)]. The existing effect at :221 cannot be reused — it returns early unless status === "found", so it never sees a failure.

PII rules for this task

  • Never put the copied string in project_shared segmentation. All three embed the project key: publicProjectUrl (src/lib/preview/publish.ts:25), embedProjectUrl (:35), embedCode (:41). That key is the live public access credential for a customer's map.
  • Never send result.error from publish verbatim — on a 403 it is a backend message that names the owner, and owner_email rides beside it (src/lib/projects/projectActionResult.ts:40-43).
  • Never send the project name, address, or lat/lng from NewProjectFlow (:124-128) — a real building address and 6-decimal coordinates.
  • Never send the map object's title (detail.heading / info.title, PreviewOverlay.tsx:610-630) — customer content, unbounded cardinality. "Top viewed places" is a tempting feature but it is a deliberate product decision, not a side effect of this task.
  • Never send the route path or endpoint coordinates (routeResult.segments[].path, converted to real lng/lat at multiLevelRoute.ts:193) — that is a precise indoor movement trace inside an identifiable building.

Acceptance criteria

  • Opening a published map reports indoor_map_opened with the right surface and framing, including inside a tour iframe.
  • Publish and unpublish from both surfaces report the matching action and surface.
  • Copying each of the three share strings reports the matching channel, and no URL or key reaches Countly.
  • Planning a route that fails reports the specific failure status, not silence.

All six events are in, merged to development via #710. New reporters: src/lib/analytics/viewerEvent.ts, publishEvent.ts, shareEvent.ts, previewEvent.ts.

NewProjectFlow only ever creates an empty-canvas project: the scan card is router.push("/start") and creates nothing, and the component has no import path. workflow would be a constant on every row. entry_source loses wizard for the same reason — the component is mounted in exactly two places, neither the wizard. Those flows already report wizard_location_confirmed (#698) and floor_plan_import (#699), so a second report here would double-count. The spec also described only the success path; result: error needs the catch, so there are two calls.

directions_route_planned — cross_level cannot be transfers.length > 0. RouteTransfer.kind is VerticalAccessType | "outdoor" and a cross-building route always appends an outdoor transfer, so a purely horizontal trip between two ground floors would have reported as vertical. Split into cross_level (any non-outdoor) and cross_building (any outdoor). The effect is also not keyed on routeKey alone: that omits fromMode and the dropped pin's point, so re-dropping the pin on the same floor changes the route but not the key.

The catch is a third reachable failure exit the spec missed. The report sits after hydratePersistedState because that call is inside the same try; before it, one page load could emit both an available and an unavailable row. framing reuses isGothruTourReferrer (tourBridge.ts) rather than a second frame check.

The copy handler did not need threading: useCopy is invoked once per section, so the channel is a literal at each. renameSweep.test.ts was updated for the new required prop — a typecheck break, not a test-run break, as suspected.

issues.display_title: Issue #702: Analytics: sign-in, sign-up, and email activation events (Countly)
issues.main_description_html:
Instrument authentication — sign-in, sign-up, and email activation. From the event inventory run against #696. Depends on the trackEvent helper landing in the wizard-funnel task.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Why

Nothing currently distinguishes a failed login from a bounce; only the /login view exists. And email verification is a hard gate — src/proxy.ts:43-49 redirects unverified users away from /start and /editor, so an account that never activates is an account that never reaches the product at all. That drop-off is invisible today.

Note that loginAction (src/actions/auth.ts:9) and registerAction (:31) are "use server" actions and cannot report — every event below fires from the client component that awaits them.

Events

sign_in

  • Call sites: src/app/(auth)/login/login-form.tsx:40 (after await loginAction — success at :59, EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED at :43, generic failure at :50) and src/components/auth/GoogleSignInButton.tsx:46 (the signIn("google") redirect).
  • Segmentation: provider: credentials | google · outcome: success | invalid_credentials | email_not_verified | server_error | started | provider_error · surface: login | register.

sign_up

  • Call sites, all in src/app/(auth)/register/register-form.tsx: :67 (setCreated(true)) → created; :63, inside the if ("error" in result) block before the return → rejected_api; :55, the if (!passwordLongEnough) early return → rejected_password.
  • Segmentation: outcome: created | rejected_password | rejected_api. One key, three bounded values, no free text, no provider segment.

account_activation

  • Call sites: src/app/(auth)/verify-email/verify-email-client.tsx — one call inside the .then at :32-41, placed before the await update() on :39 so a failed session refresh cannot swallow the report, and one in the existing if (!token) return early return at :25-26 (not at :21, which is a useState initializer). Resend paths: src/app/(auth)/verify-email-pending/verify-pending-client.tsx:66 (sent), :59 (rate-limited), :63 (failed).
  • Segmentation: step: link_opened | resend_requested · outcome: verified | invalid_link | missing_token | sent | rate_limited | failed. Twelve combinations at most, no ids, no free text.

PII rules for this task — the strictest in the whole analytics effort

  • email and password are both in scope at login-form.tsx:40. fullName, email and password are locals at register-form.tsx:31-33, passed at :59. None of them may appear in any segmentation value, ever.
  • The activation token is a single-use credential and it is sitting in scope as token at verify-email-client.tsx:19. It must never reach Countly — not as a segment, not in an error string, not via the view name.
  • Never segment on result.error (register-form.tsx:62) — Go server text, unbounded, and it can echo the submitted email back.

Acceptance criteria

  • Each outcome above is reachable and reports the right bounded value — verify email_not_verified and rate_limited specifically, since they are the two that matter and the two easiest to miss.
  • No email, name, password, or token appears in any event payload. Check the actual network request, not just the code.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

All three events are in, merged to development via #711. New reporter: src/lib/analytics/authEvent.ts.

Event Where it fires
sign_in login-form.tsx — one call covering success and the three bucketed failures; GoogleSignInButton.tsx for started; a mount effect in login-form.tsx for provider_error
sign_up register-form.tsx — rejected_password at the length guard, rejected_api in the error branch, created after setCreated(true)
account_activation verify-email-client.tsx for link_opened (verified / invalid_link / missing_token); verify-pending-client.tsx for resend_requested (sent / rate_limited / failed)

Everything specified above was confirmed against the tree

All the cited line numbers and branches were real. Three things needed a decision the issue did not cover:

  1. Google needs both halves reported from different files. GoogleSignInButton hands the browser to Google with a full-page redirect and never regains control, so started is all it can observe. The failure returns as ?error= on the login page — that is where provider_error is reported, behind a ref so StrictMode's second effect pass does not double it.
  2. GoogleSignInButton gained a required surface prop. It is rendered on both /login and /register and had no way to say which. Both call sites updated; there are no others.
  3. Two placements are load-bearing. The verified report fires before await update(), so a failing session refresh cannot swallow the one signal that the account activated — exactly as the issue asked. The missing_token report uses its own ref rather than the existing single-use-token guard (ranRef), so it cannot block a token arriving on a later effect pass.

Privacy

The reporters take no free-text parameter at all. That is the guarantee rather than a convention: there is no argument through which a caller could pass an email, a full name, a password or the activation token. Every outcome is bucketed at the call site by comparing against a known literal — "EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED", "Invalid email or password", "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS" — and no backend string is ever forwarded, since those can echo the submitted address back. The activation token is a single-use credential and is never read into an event.

Tests

src/lib/analytics/__tests__/authEvent.test.ts — 5 cases, including one asserting the wire payload of all three reporters contains no @, no token, no password and no name fragment.

Verification

issues.main_description_html:
The virtual-tour embed link the product hands out is blocked by the browser before any JavaScript runs.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What is broken

next.config.ts serves two header sets. The permissive one — frame-ancestors *, no X-Frame-Options — is matched by source: "/v/:path+". The strict one is everything else, matched by the lookahead source: "/((?!v/).*)", and it sends frame-ancestors 'self' plus X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN.

/embed/[key] fell into the strict branch. It is a public embeddable viewer — src/app/embed/[key]/page.tsx is nothing but <LivePage embedded />, the same component /v/[key] renders, with the information card hidden because the tour player owns info display (#315).

The share modal hands that exact URL to the user as the virtual-tour embed link: embedProjectUrl(projectKey, origin) in src/lib/preview/publish.ts builds /embed/<key>, and PreviewShareModal's EmbedTourSection presents it for copying. So a tour on tourmkr.com that iframes the link this product generated is refused by the browser — no request reaches the app, nothing renders, and there is no error the user can act on.

The website-embed snippet is unaffected: embedCode() wraps publicProjectUrl = /v/<key>, which is in the permissive branch.

Found while mapping call sites for the indoor_map_opened analytics event (#701). Worth fixing first on its own merits, and also because the event would otherwise report "nobody uses the tour embed" when the truth is "the browser blocks it".

Fix

Exempt /embed the same way /v is exempted, and give it the same permissive header set.

source: "/((?!v/|embed/).*)"   // was "/((?!v/).*)"

plus a /embed/:path+ entry using securityHeaders("*").

The lookahead is written as (?!v/|embed/) rather than (?!v|embed) so a path that merely starts with those letters — /embedded-anything — keeps the strict policy.

Acceptance criteria

  • curl -I https://<host>/embed/<key> returns no X-Frame-Options header and frame-ancestors * in the CSP.
  • /dashboard, /editor/<id> and / still return X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN and frame-ancestors 'self'.
  • A tour player on tourmkr.com successfully iframes the embed link copied from the share modal.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #712: Analytics phase 2a: wizard step-3 usage, resume, and the JSON escape hatches (Countly)

The wizard half of the phase-2 event set (#703), plus the one ingestion gap #698 left behind.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

wizard_step_entered (#698) says where people drop out. These say why step 3 exists and whether the power-user paths around generation are real.

floor_config_edited

Tells you whether step 3 (Order) is real work or a pass-through tax. If almost nobody renames, re-heights or reorders, the step is pure friction between upload and generate and could default-skip; if they do, the auto-naming/same-height toggles are earning their keep. One key with an action segment beats five near-duplicate keys.

  • Call site: src/components/setup/StepListFloor.tsx:135 (handleReorder — the single commit point for BOTH reorder surfaces, the list and the modal), :204 (onSettingsChange → setFloorSettings), :205 (onFloorChange → updateFloorConfig, name/height), :206 (onFloorDelete → removeFloorConfig). The modal is step-list-floor/EditFloorModal.tsx, opened from #btn-edit-floors (step-list-floor/FloorList.tsx:49).

Compare the id order before firing (and before the store write — it is a wasted setCanvasData today either way). Note keyboard reorder (useFloorReorder.ts:93) fires once per arrow keypress, so a four-slot keyboard move reads as four reorders.

Guard the unit case with u !== unit; :352 fires on clicking the already-active unit.

The two power-user escape hatches around generation: loading a previously generated project JSON instead of scanning, and downloading the result. Low volume by design, but the loader has a real rejection path (StepGenerate.tsx:211 rejects anything missing place_info/levels) and the download is the strongest signal a user considered the generated Digital Twin good enough to keep.

  • Call site: src/components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx:201 — handleJsonUpload; success at line 215 (setGeneratedTwin), rejections at lines 212 (missing place_info/levels), 217 (parse error), 220 (read error). Download: src/components/setup/step-generate/GenerateProcessSummary.tsx:131 (#btn-download-json), wired to downloadJson at StepGenerate.tsx:296 → src/hooks/useDigitalTwinExport.ts:57.

#698 shipped this key for the wizard's step 2 only. The same upload runs from the editor's Add Floor flow at src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts:72, and it is currently unreported, so the dashboard's upload failure rate silently excludes it.

  • Change: add a source: wizard_step2 | editor_add_floor segment to the existing reportUpload in src/lib/analytics/uploadEvent.ts and call it from the editor path with the same outcome buckets.

  • No id, file name, floor name, share key, email, address, coordinate or raw error string reaches Countly — verify on the wire, not just in the code.

Event Where it fires

issues.display_title: Issue #713: Analytics phase 2b: map-editor georeferencing events (Countly)
issues.main_description_html:
The map-editor half of the phase-2 event set (#703): the gestures that put a building where it really is.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Georeferencing is the core map-mode gesture and #700 covers only which tool was selected, not whether it was used or how. These four say whether the alignment tools earn their place.

Same rules as #698–#702, which are all merged: fire from the client (server actions cannot reach the SDK), reuse trackEvent and the bucket helpers in src/lib/analytics/events.ts, put anything with branch logic in its own reporter module beside the seven already there, and keep every segmentation value bounded — no ids, no free text, no file names, no share keys, no coordinates, no email addresses, no raw backend error strings.

Every call site below comes from the inventory sweep and was verified against the tree at the time, but #698–#702 have since edited several of these files. Re-verify each line number before editing — treat the paths as authoritative and the numbers as hints.

Events

map_placement_moved

Georeferencing the model — dragging the building/floor onto its real-world position — is the core map-editor gesture, and the one whose scope model (all buildings / building / active floor) is most likely to confuse people. Fires once per completed drag: useBuildingDrag commits exactly one write on mouseup (useBuildingDrag.ts:171-179 endDrag → onCommit), so volume is one event per gesture, not per mousemove. The floor-stack snap result (#594) is a property of this gesture, so it belongs here as segmentation rather than as its own key. Wrap the onCommit: commitDrag prop — commitDrag itself (Editor3DMapView.tsx:242) is shared with the wall-vertex path, so firing inside it would conflate two different actions.

  • Call site: src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx:274
  • Segmentation: scope: allBuildings|building|floor · snap: off|armed|matched
  • PII: HIGH if you send the placement itself. The drag produces lng/lat deltas against the project location (useBuildingDrag.ts:124-128) — the project location is a real building address. Send NO coordinates, no offsets, no lat/lng, no level_id.

map_wall_point_moved

Wall-point editing on the map (#688) plus the previous-floor snap (#689) are the newest geometry features and the ones with the most recent bug traffic (commits e9d405c / 5c174c4). One event per committed drag tells you whether the mode is used at all and how often the snap actually catches — the whole justification for #689. The overlay already guarantees one commit per gesture (dead zone at MapWallVertexHandles.tsx:20, single onCommitVertex at :243), so this cannot become per-frame volume.

  • Call site: src/components/editor/map-wall-edit/MapWallVertexHandles.tsx:243
  • Segmentation: snapped: "vertex" | "segment" | "none" (bounded union — SnapTarget.kind is declared "vertex" | "segment" at src/lib/map/wall-vertex-edit.ts:69; today it is only written to a DOM attr at MapWallVertexHandles.tsx:230 and stripped at :239, so add snapped to dragRef at :232 alongside d.last) · alt_free: true|false (e.altKey is read per move at :226 and never persisted — this needs a SECOND dragRef field, not the one the proposal budgeted) · snap_available: true|false (replaces has_floor_below; the proposal's "d.targets non-empty" test is wrong — targets is always an object, {vertices: [], segments: []} when there is no floor below (:210), so the check must be d.targets.vertices.length + d.targets.segments.length > 0). 12 bounded combos, no ids. NO x/y, no wallId (nanoid, unbounded), no level_id, no project id.
  • PII: Do not send x/y model pixels or the wallId (nanoid, unbounded cardinality). Counts and enums only.

map_placement_transformed

The rotate/scale/nudge/reset popup is the fine-alignment half of georeferencing and is easy to miss entirely — a single key with an action dimension says whether it is discovered and which control does the work. Crucially the events must sit on the COMMIT, not the drag: handleRotate/handleScale run per mousemove via setCanvasDataSilent (MapTransformControl.tsx:190/216), so only handleDragEnd (:168) is safe. The nudge D-pad and Reset are already single-shot commits.

  • Call site: src/components/editor/MapTransformControl.tsx:385
  • Segmentation: action: rotate|scale|nudge|reset|drag · scope: allBuildings|building|floor. No magnitude. 15 bounded combos, no ids. Fire points: rotate at MapTransformControl.tsx:385 and scale at :398 (wrap the onDragEnd prop — handleDragEnd at :168 cannot tell them apart, as claimed); nudge at :413/:423/:435/:445; reset at :494; drag at useBuildingDrag.ts:172. Nudge must be coalesced: one event per burst via trailing debounce, using Countly's native count field, not one event per D-pad click.
  • PII: None if bucketed; do not send raw rotationDeg/scale/offset values — they describe a specific real-world placement.

editor_view_changed

Two toggles, one question: which representation people actually work in. The Editor/Map tab switch is the top-level mode of the whole editor (2D drawing vs georeferenced 3D map), and the 3D-panel toggle inside the floor-plan editor is the '3D preview' switch. Merging them into one key with a surface dimension avoids two near-duplicate keys, and both are cheap (a deliberate click, a handful per session). The 3D panel toggle also has a perf story attached — the paused render loop (#675, editor/index.ts:106-107).

  • Call site: src/components/editor/EditorCanvas.tsx:75
  • Segmentation: view: canvas_editor | canvas_3d | panel_3d_shown | panel_3d_hidden — one bounded key, four disjoint self-describing values. canvas_* fired from src/components/editor/EditorCanvas.tsx:75 as canvas_${btn.id} (guarded by btn.id !== canvasFilter); panel_3d_* fired from toggle3D in src/components/editor/FloorplanEditor.tsx:569 as panel_3d_${!p.view ? "shown" : "hidden"}. Drop the separate surface dimension.

Acceptance criteria

  • Every event reports with the exact key and bounded values listed.
  • No id, file name, floor name, share key, email, address, coordinate or raw error string reaches Countly — verify on the wire, not just in the code.
  • Each reporter with real branch logic has a test that fails when the branch is broken.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

All four are in, merged to development via #718. New reporter: src/lib/analytics/mapEditEvent.ts.

Three of the four are pointer gestures, so the whole problem was volume. Each reports once per completed gesture, from the commit. The per-pixel handlers deliberately left alone: useBuildingDrag's onMouseMove, MapWallVertexHandles's onPointerMove, and the window mousemove listeners inside RotateKnob / ScaleHandle.

Event Commit point
map_placement_moved useBuildingDrag.ts endDrag → the onCommit arrow in Editor3DMapView.tsx
map_placement_transformed MapTransformControl.tsx handleDragEnd (rotate/scale), handleNudge, handleReset
map_wall_point_moved MapWallVertexHandles.tsx onPointerUp, inside the d.moved branch
editor_view_changed EditorCanvas.tsx tab click; FloorplanEditor.tsx toggle3D

What the code forced

  • onCommit was widened to (data, { frame, distanceM }). Only the hook knows which frame the drag wrote and how far it travelled — the branch is taken there and the metres are already computed for the transform. The alternative was a canvas diff plus a copy of the frame-selection logic in the component.
  • The report sits on the onCommit arrow, not inside commitDrag. That callback is shared with the wall-vertex drag; instrumenting the body would count every vertex edit as a building placement, in a mutually exclusive mode.
  • scope and frame are separate dimensions. Scope is what the user asked for, frame is what the geometry allowed — a floor-scoped drag on a project with no buildings writes the project frame.
  • Rotate and scale are gated on the canvas identity changing. handleDragEnd has no such check, so a stray click on the knob already pushes a duplicate history entry; without the gate it would also report a rotation that rotated nothing.
  • scope reaches handleDragEnd from the render site, not scopeRef. Reading the ref there makes react-hooks/immutability reject the pre-existing mirror effect.
  • The wall-vertex gesture object now carries the snap result. It exists only in the per-move handler, so the last move's snap kind and Alt state are written on the same lines as the coordinate they describe.
  • editor_view_changed reports before setPanels, not inside the updater — React invokes updaters twice under StrictMode. The canvas tab is gated on the value actually changing. The mount state is deliberately not reported: a near-constant would drown the real switches, and indoor_map_opened already counts opens.

Intended reading, not a bug

A drag that returns to its own starting pixel still commits and still reports — every move builds a fresh object, so the identity guard cannot tell the numbers are unchanged. Both drag events count gestures performed; the <1 metre bucket is exactly the "armed the tool, wobbled, committed nothing" population.

Tests

src/lib/analytics/__tests__/mapEditEvent.test.ts — 10 cases: every distance bucket boundary, scope-vs-frame kept separate, a check that no raw distance reaches the payload, the snap/override pair, and the transform and view payloads.

Privacy

No coordinates and no ids. e.lngLat, startLngLat and the project location are all in scope at the commit; only their difference, as a scalar magnitude in metres and then bucketed, is reported.

Verification

pnpm test 1336 passed / 3 skipped (157 files) · pnpm lint clean with zero warnings · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #714: Analytics phase 2c: 2D editor rework and edit-volume events (Countly)
issues.main_description_html:
The 2D-editor half of the phase-2 event set (#703): how much of what the AI produces gets thrown away, and how much mapping actually gets done.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

geometry_deleted and edit_history_step are the sharpest proxies for scan quality the product can produce without asking anyone. indoor_map_edit_summary answers "how much work happened" without an event per save — the editor autosaves 2 seconds after every edit burst, so a per-save event would dwarf everything else in the app.

Same rules as #698–#702, which are all merged: fire from the client (server actions cannot reach the SDK), reuse trackEvent and the bucket helpers in src/lib/analytics/events.ts, put anything with branch logic in its own reporter module beside the seven already there, and keep every segmentation value bounded — no ids, no free text, no file names, no share keys, no coordinates, no email addresses, no raw backend error strings.

Every call site below comes from the inventory sweep and was verified against the tree at the time, but #698–#702 have since edited several of these files. Re-verify each line number before editing — treat the paths as authoritative and the numbers as hints.

Events

geometry_deleted

How much of what the AI scan produces gets thrown away — the sharpest available proxy for scan quality, and a direct read on rework. deleteSelected is the single choke point every delete path funnels through: the Del/Backspace key (interactions.ts:598), the toolbar trash buttons (SelectionToolbars.tsx:183, :295), and all four sidebar-row deletes (commands.ts:140-183 deleteWallAt / deleteOpeningAt / deleteAnnotationAt / deleteShapeAt each end in deleteSelected). One event, one site.

  • Call site: src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/commands.ts:29
  • Segmentation: segmentation: { kind: "wall" | "opening" | "manual_area" | "annotation" | "shape" } — 5 bounded values, one per else-if branch (commands.ts:31/32/33/34/44). Nothing else in segmentation.

count/sum: send count: 1, sum: — NOT count: n as proposed. Countly's Events report renders Count and Sum as separate columns; folding the item count into count destroys "how many delete actions happened" (the per-session behavioural number) and inflates the graph whenever someone marquee-selects. count=1/sum=n gives both readings for free. Items = ctx.selWalls.length | ctx.selOps.length | 1 | ctx.selAnnos.length | ctx.selShapes.length, captured BEFORE the branch clears the array.

Explicitly forbidden in segmentation (all would be PII or unbounded-cardinality): wall/shape/annotation ids (nanoid — unbounded, blows up the Events report), x/y coordinates (a digital twin is a real building; coordinates plus a project id locate a person's desk), project id, level/floor id, room or annotation labels (user-authored free text).

Known losses, accepted deliberately: "opening" merges doors and windows because ctx.selOps is one mixed array (commands.ts:32 filters model.doors and model.windows separately) — add a door/window split only if that distinction ever gets asked for. "annotation" likewise merges points/safety/access (commands.ts:36-40). No via: key|toolbar|sidebar source segment — it would mean threading a param through four call sites for a question nobody has asked; add it when someone asks whether the sidebar row-delete is discoverable.

  • PII: None as long as it stays kind + count. No ids, no coordinates.

edit_history_step

Undo/redo rate is the standard read on how error-prone an editing tool is, and this app has TWO independent history stacks that users cannot tell apart — the floor-plan engine's JSON-snapshot stack (history.ts:64/69, persisted per level in localStorage) and the map editor's canvasHistory (editorSlice.ts:310/322). Segmenting by surface tells you which half of the editor people are fighting. Both stacks already return early on an empty stack, so the event only fires on a real revert. Volume is user-paced but can burst on a held Ctrl+Z.

  • Call site: src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/history.ts:64
  • Segmentation: action: undo|redo · surface: floor_plan|map_geometry — two segments, 4 bounded combinations. Fire at the two verified choke points: src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/history.ts:64 (undo) / :69 (redo) with surface="floor_plan", and src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts:310 (undo) / :322 (redo) with surface="map_geometry". DROP via from v1: the choke points cannot see it, and threading it through requires touching the engine's undo(ctx) signature, the Zustand action type at editorSlice.ts:94-95, and all four callers — a 4-file diff for a dimension that only answers "do people find the toolbar buttons". Add it later as an optional third arg if toolbar discoverability becomes a question. Do NOT add project_id, level_id, or historyKey — they are unbounded and would wreck the Events report; the localStorage key at history.ts:18 (fp_history:${key}) is right there and must not be segmented on. Implementation wrinkle: both map-side sites sit INSIDE a Zustand set((s) => ...) updater, after the guards at editorSlice.ts:311 and :323. Zustand invokes the updater once so firing there works, but the tidier placement is to read historyIndex/canvasHistory.length via get() before calling set(). PII: none — no ids, no coordinates, no paths, no share keys.

floorplan_edit_blocked

Every 'you can't do that' message in the 2D editor already flows through one callback with an explicit error flag — status(m, err=true). Firing only on err===true gives a free friction feed: 'a door can only be added on a wall' (interactions.ts:217), 'not on a straight wall, not a curved one' (:218), 'nothing to paste' (commands.ts:95), 'select door(s)/window(s) to align' (:107), 'selected opening(s) are not on a wall' (:109), 'nothing to download/export' (:14/:21), and the .txt parse failure (model-sync.ts:214). These are the moments a user's intent was rejected, and none are observable today.

  • Call site: src/components/editor/FloorplanEditor.tsx:282
  • Segmentation: reason: bucketed enum via a substring-match table at FloorplanEditor.tsx:282 (never the raw message) — opening_needs_wall (interactions.ts:217) | opening_needs_straight_wall (:218) | opening_not_on_wall (commands.ts:109) | no_selection (commands.ts:88, :107, :115) | nothing_to_paste (commands.ts:95) | no_model (commands.ts:14, :21) | parse_error (model-sync.ts:214, message discarded) | other (mandatory fallback so future strings surface instead of vanishing). Optional bounded second segment: opening_kind = door|window, captured from the same match on interactions.ts:217-218. No ids, no coordinates, no file names, no user-supplied text.

map_object_information_link

Attaching an Information record to a wall/area/door/point is the step that turns map geometry into a digital twin, and the panel supports both a bulk link over a whole selection (SelectedFeaturePanel.tsx:153-157, with a >=10 confirmation gate at :161) and single-row unlink (:444) / unlink-all (:380). add_event({

segmentation: {

The answer to 'how much mapping actually got done' WITHOUT an event per save. Read the counts off useMapStore.getState() immediately BEFORE the reset() on line 41.

  • Every event reports with the exact key and bounded values listed.
  • No id, file name, floor name, share key, email, address, coordinate or raw error string reaches Countly — verify on the wire, not just in the code.
  • Each reporter with real branch logic has a test that fails when the branch is broken.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

Five of the six are in, merged to development via #719. New reporters: src/lib/analytics/editEvent.ts and src/lib/analytics/editSummaryEvent.ts.

None of the reporting is in the engine

commands.ts, history.ts, selection.ts and model-sync.ts are pure and directly unit-tested, and those suites build a partial callbacks object behind a cast precisely to keep side-effect dependencies out. Two optional taps were added to the existing bus — deleted and historyStep, both called with ?. — and the reporting happens in FloorplanEditor, the route #700 already used for mode. No existing test needed editing.

Worth recording so nobody argues the other way from a green test run: trackEvent is a silent no-op under the node test env, so putting the SDK straight into those modules would have kept every test passing and still been wrong.

Routing through the bus rather than the two toolbar buttons also covers the keyboard shortcuts, which call history.ts directly and bypass the engine facade.

What the code forced

  • floorplan_edit_blocked reports a code, never the message. Three of the ten raise sites build their text dynamically — two interpolate the armed tool, one concatenates a parser error raised over customer file content — so the message is neither bounded nor stable, and the other seven are UI copy a rewording would fork. status() gained an optional trailing reason; all ten sites pass one.
  • map_object_information_link would have shipped a mislabelling. For ten or more objects the link goes through a confirm dialog, and setCreating(false) has already run by the time "Link all" is pressed — so reading creating inside doLink reports a brand-new record as existing, and only for large selections. The origin now travels with the pending confirmation.
  • Walls are not linkable. The linkable set is MarkerKind, not "wall/area/door/point" as this issue said; a mixed selection reports kind: "mixed".
  • The map history stack is gated on the same conditions the buttons are disabled by. The store's undo/redo are no-ops at the ends of the stack and the keyboard path has no guard, so an unconditional report would count keystrokes that changed nothing.
  • indoor_map_edit_summary is honest about its coverage. One row per session, zero during editing. It measures sessions that ended by navigating out of the editor: a tab close, a reload or a typed URL never runs the unmount that ends the session, and the SDK drains its queue over XHR on a timer so a pagehide hook could not reliably flush one either. Those sessions are missing rather than zero, and the helper's doc says so. It hangs off the deferred reset that already tells a real exit from the Editor ⇄ Preview hop, so one visit to preview and back stays one session.

Tests

src/lib/analytics/__tests__/editEvent.test.ts — 13 cases: all five delete kinds and the sum/bucket split, the two history stacks kept apart, the blocked code, the bulk-link collapse and the unlink direction, and three session cases driven against a real store (nothing reported without a session, the signed object delta and level bucket, and the same project not restarting a session).

Privacy

No ids, names, titles, descriptions, file content or error text. Deletions and links report a kind and a count; the summary reports buckets, a role and a status.
