issues.display_title: Issue #715: Analytics phase 2d: published-map wayfinding and project lifecycle events (Countly)
issues.main_description_html:
The viewer and lifecycle half of the phase-2 event set (#703).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

place_search is the most actionable event in the whole inventory: a zero-result search on a published map is a visitor asking for something the customer never labelled. tour_panorama_sync is the only visibility into a cross-product integration that currently has none.

Same rules as #698–#702, which are all merged: fire from the client (server actions cannot reach the SDK), reuse trackEvent and the bucket helpers in src/lib/analytics/events.ts, put anything with branch logic in its own reporter module beside the seven already there, and keep every segmentation value bounded — no ids, no free text, no file names, no share keys, no coordinates, no email addresses, no raw backend error strings.

Every call site below comes from the inventory sweep and was verified against the tree at the time, but #698–#702 have since edited several of these files. Re-verify each line number before editing — treat the paths as authoritative and the numbers as hints.

Events

place_search

Zero-result searches are the single most actionable signal a published indoor map produces: visitors are asking for something the customer never labelled. Nothing else in the app surfaces that.

  • Call site: src/components/editor/preview/SearchAreaPanel.tsx:65 (onChange → setQuery) — needs a debounce wrapper, and note the deliberate ponytail comment at :29 explaining why there is none today (matching is a synchronous in-memory filter)
  • Segmentation: result_count: "0" | "1-5" | "6+" (from results.length, SearchAreaPanel.tsx:38-42) · surface: "editor" | "preview" | "live" | "embed" (new prop threaded from PreviewOverlay's existing standalone/live/embedded flags, PreviewOverlay.tsx:49). Two keys, 12 bounded combos. NEVER the query string. Drop has_category. Guard: do not fire when targets.length === 0.
  • PII: NEVER send the query string. It is visitor-typed free text on an unauthenticated public page — it can contain a person's name, a phone number, anything. Only the bucketed count is safe. This candidate is worth shipping only if that constraint is respected; otherwise skip it.

wayfinding_tool_opened

Do visitors on a published map ever reach for Search Area or Direction, or do they only pan around? Cheapest possible read on whether the wayfinding features earn their screen space.

  • Call site: src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx:729 (onToggleSearch) and :734 (onToggleDirection), both passed to PreviewControls
  • Segmentation: tool: search|direction; surface: live|embed|preview|editor (four PreviewOverlay mounts — editor overlay must be separable from visitor surfaces). Fire on OPEN only — drop the opened|closed state segment, since PreviewOverlay.tsx:264 closes the feature outside both handlers and would undercount closes. Optional, only if outdoor/overview mode is live: outdoor: true|false, because the Direction button is not rendered when outdoor (PreviewControls.tsx:82). Never segment by projectId or the /v/[key] share key.

tour_panorama_sync

The GoThru virtual-tour embed is a cross-product integration with zero field visibility today. This says whether the postMessage bridge is actually exchanging panoramas in production, and how often an inbound panorama has no matching map marker — the silent no-op that would otherwise look like "the map is broken" to the tour's users.

  • Call site: src/components/editor/preview/useTourSync.ts:81 (selectRef → sync.selectMarker, outbound map→tour, reaching tourBridge.ts:121 postSelect) and :70/:74 (setActive/center callbacks — the inbound tour→map path; the no-match no-op is src/lib/preview/tourSync.ts:73)
  • Segmentation: direction: "map_to_tour" | "tour_to_map"; matched: true | false; level_switched: true | false (false whenever N/A — outbound, or inbound on the already-active floor). 2x2x2 = 8 bounded combos, no ids. Explicitly NOT sent: tourKey, panoramaId, markerId, level_id, lng/lat.
  • PII: Do not send tourKey (PanoMarker.tourKey, src/lib/preview/panoMarkers.ts:12, emitted on the wire at tourBridge.ts:123) — it identifies a specific customer's GoThru virtual tour, the same class of public-but-linkable identifier as project_key. panoramaId alone is high-cardinality and answers no product question; direction + matched is the whole signal. IMPORTANT: fire from useTourSync.ts, never from tourBridge.ts or tourSync.ts — those are deliberately pure, injectable, unit-tested modules (see their headers), and the SDK is browser-only anyway.

project_lifecycle

Duplicate is a discovered power-user workflow (fork a published map to iterate safely); delete of a published project is a churn signal. Both are cheap to fold into one key rather than two near-identical ones.

  • Call site: src/app/dashboard/useDashboard.ts:203 (deleteProject) and :233 (duplicateProject)
  • Segmentation: action: publish | unpublish | delete | duplicate (from the three handlers at useDashboard.ts:156, :196, :230 — reuse the OwnerOnlyAction union already declared at src/lib/collaboration/ownerGuard.ts:7 so the values stay in sync); result: ok | error | threw (the three real branches — result.ok true, result.ok false, and the catch); reason: forbidden | failed, sent only when result is "error" — derive with "owner_email" in result (the only 403 signal that survives projectActionFailure, projectActionResult.ts:41-43), NEVER pass result.error through; was_published: boolean from p.status === "published" on the Project param at :196 / :230. Dropped from the proposal: surface (single-valued — dashboard is the only caller), blocked_not_owner (belongs in the existing recordOwnerOnlyBlocked stub at ownerGuard.ts:25 as its own owner_only_action_blocked event with an action segment). Never send: result.error, owner_email, projectName(project), p.id, project.project_key. Not a timed event. Fires from the client hook — src/actions/projects.ts is "use server" and cannot.
  • PII: Same trap as project_published: result.error on a 403 can contain the owner's email (projectActionResult.ts:40-43). Map to a bounded code. Do not send the project name (ProjectViews.tsx:204/:224 renders it in the confirm copy) — it is customer content with unbounded cardinality.

Acceptance criteria

  • Every event reports with the exact key and bounded values listed.
  • No id, file name, floor name, share key, email, address, coordinate or raw error string reaches Countly — verify on the wire, not just in the code.
  • Each reporter with real branch logic has a test that fails when the branch is broken.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

All four are in, merged to development via #720. New reporter src/lib/analytics/tourSyncEvent.ts; the other three extend previewEvent.ts and publishEvent.ts.

Event Where it fires
place_search SearchAreaPanel.tsx, a 600 ms trailing timer keyed on the trimmed term
wayfinding_tool_opened PreviewOverlay.tsx — both toolbar toggles and the info card's Direction button
tour_panorama_sync lib/preview/tourSync.ts, inbound and outbound, after the bridge's loop guard
project_lifecycle useDashboard.ts handleDelete / handleDuplicate, all six exits

The query is not reported — a deliberate, flagged loss

This issue called the zero-result term the most actionable signal in the inventory. The rate ships; the term does not, in any form.

That text is arbitrary input from a stranger on a public page, and the visitor is a data subject nobody onboarded. The coarse middle ground — a length bucket, a has-digits flag — is the worst option: nothing a customer could act on, full privacy cost. The right home for the terms is a server-side, per-project, length-capped zero-result log with a retention policy; that is a product decision, not a Countly segmentation key. Same reasoning previewEvent.ts already uses for declining to report object titles. Raised for a product call rather than decided quietly.

What the code forced

  • The search panel has no debounce, by design — the filter is a synchronous in-memory match and says so in a comment. The event had to create its own boundary or "toilet" would be six prefix rows. 600 ms trailing, keyed on the trimmed term: an ordinary visitor minute drops from 15–25 rows to 2–3.
  • Browsing a category is not a search. results is also non-null for an open category, and empty categories are filtered out before rendering — so a browse row always carries ≥1 hit and would have quietly deflated the zero-result rate.
  • tour_panorama_sync must sit after the loop guard. At the message layer it would catch the raw firehose (~60 messages/second during a look-around drag). It is not debounced and must not be: the guard is last-id-only, so A → B → A is three real steps.
  • Only the presence of a tour key travels. The marker builder defaults it to "", and a tour handed an empty key has nothing to resolve against — a live, currently invisible way for the outbound half to do nothing.
  • wayfinding_tool_opened reports the open transition only. The info card stays on screen during direction mode and its button never disables, so a second press would otherwise report a second discovery.
  • project_lifecycle keeps the raw backend status, so "deleted while unpublished" stays distinct from "deleted while never published". The report lives in the dashboard hook, not the row component: design-preview/collaboration renders the real rows with no-op handlers against published fixtures, and moving it outward would turn every designer click into a fake success row.

Tests

src/lib/analytics/__tests__/viewerLifecycleEvents.test.ts — 12 cases: the zero-results bucket and every boundary above it, an assertion that the search reporter has no parameter a query could arrive through, the wayfinding source split, the tour-key flag present on send and absent inbound, and the lifecycle status/result pair.

Verification

issues.main_description_html:
The account half of the phase-2 event set (#703).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

sign_out matters less as a metric than as the correct place to unbind the Countly identity, so it should land whenever identity binding does. subscription_checkout is the only monetization funnel that exists in code.

The PII rules from #702 apply in full here: reporters for these paths should take no free-text parameter at all, so there is no argument an email or a token could travel through.

Same rules as #698–#702, which are all merged: fire from the client (server actions cannot reach the SDK), reuse trackEvent and the bucket helpers in src/lib/analytics/events.ts, put anything with branch logic in its own reporter module beside the seven already there, and keep every segmentation value bounded — no ids, no free text, no file names, no share keys, no coordinates, no email addresses, no raw backend error strings.

Every call site below comes from the inventory sweep and was verified against the tree at the time, but #698–#702 have since edited several of these files. Re-verify each line number before editing — treat the paths as authoritative and the numbers as hints.

Events

account_password

Whether locked-out users actually get back in — request sent vs link opened vs reset completed is a three-step funnel today measured by nothing. Same key covers the signed-in password change so security-hygiene volume is visible in one place.

  • Call site: src/app/(auth)/forgot-password/forgot-password-form.tsx:25 (setStage("sent")); src/app/(auth)/reset-password/reset-password-form.tsx:50 (token validation result), :88 (reset completed), :80 (token died between validate and submit); src/app/profile/profile-client.tsx:297 (signed-in change)
  • Segmentation: step: reset_requested | reset_link_opened | reset_submitted | changed_signed_in · outcome: ok | invalid_link | failed. Bounded at 4x3. Fire points: reset_requested at forgot-password-form.tsx:25 (outcome always ok, by design); reset_link_opened at reset-password-form.tsx:50 (ok | invalid_link); reset_submitted at :88 (ok), :80 (invalid_link), :84 (failed — MISSING from the proposal, this is the real generic-failure branch); changed_signed_in at profile-client.tsx:304 (ok) and :299 (failed) — NOT :297 as proposed, which is before the result and would lose the outcome entirely. Optional 5th step value added_signed_in, gated on the isGoogleAccount boolean already in scope at profile-client.tsx:285, separates "Google user adds email login" from "security hygiene"; one ternary, different product question, take it or leave it.
  • PII: SEVERE: the reset token is in scope at reset-password-form.tsx:31 and passed at :76, and the email at forgot-password-form.tsx:20. Both are credentials/PII — segmentation gets neither. Passwords obviously never. All four underlying actions (src/actions/auth.ts:73, :83, :94, :107) are server actions and cannot report.

collab_join

Whether realtime co-editing is used at all, by whom (role), with how many people, and how stable the socket is. Access denials and disconnect churn are invisible today — nothing listens for project:error and the denied state only greys out input (FloorplanEditor.tsx:522).

  • Call site: src/lib/collab/wireCollab.ts:79 (project:joined → setJoined; has role, version, presence array) · :100 (project:denied) · :67 (socket disconnect) · session end also at src/lib/collab/useCollab.ts:51 (project:leave on unmount)

NEVER segment on: presence[] itself, Member.name / Member.userId (types.ts:4-8), the access token emitted at wireCollab.ts:56-61, or cursor x/y.
  • Timed: yes — use Countly's dur field, not start_event/end_event.
  • PII: MEDIUM: the joined payload carries presence: Member[] with userId and name (src/lib/collab/types.ts:4-8) and the join emits the raw access token (wireCollab.ts:56-61). Segment on the COUNT only — no names, no user ids, no token. projectId is an internal UUID: not PII, but unbounded cardinality; leave it out. manage_collaborators

Team growth on a project: invites sent, how many land on an address with no MapThru account (the join-invite second step), role mix, and removals. One key covers the whole access-management surface.

Call sites: :83-86 (existing open effect → action=opened, the denominator) · :142 added · :139 not_registered · :128 already_member · :156 not_owner · :159 failed · :167 sent · :170 join_invite failed · :93/:96 role_changed · :106/:115 removed. All five member actions (src/actions/members.ts:33, :47, :74, :95, :115, :134) are server actions and cannot report — the dialog is the client component ('use client', line 1).

Low analytic value on its own (track_sessions already ends the session), but the call sites are the only correct place to unbind the Countly identity — and the verify-pending variant is a real funnel signal: "Wrong email? Sign out" means the user typed the wrong address during sign-up.

  • Call site: src/components/dashboard/DashboardNav.tsx:42 (await logoutAction()) and src/app/(auth)/verify-email-pending/verify-pending-client.tsx:72
  • Segmentation: from: "dashboard" | "verify_pending" — exactly two values, nothing else. No user id, no session token.

subscription_checkout (tier: later — decide the product question first)

The only monetization funnel that exists in code: plan/add-on/credit CTA → Stripe redirect → success or cancel. Answers which surface drives checkouts and how many die at Stripe. Caveat below: it currently cannot fire in production.

  • Call site: src/app/subscription/subscription-client.tsx:33 (createCheckoutSession) and :39 (createBillingPortalSession), reached from the plan cards, the add-on button at :137 and the credit packs at :178; src/app/profile/profile-client.tsx:70 and :77; completion at src/app/billing/success/page.tsx:16 (inside the existing useEffect) and cancellation at src/app/billing/cancel/page.tsx (needs a new useEffect — the page has no effect today, only the back button at :25)

REMOVED from the proposal: outcome=completed|cancelled and the new cancel-page useEffect.
  • PII: None at these sites — no card data reaches them (the /billing form at src/app/billing/page.tsx:57 holds card number/CVC/address in local state and is an unwired layout stub; never instrument anything inside it, and never segment on country/ZIP/tax number). All three billing actions (src/actions/billing.ts:7, :27, :46) are server actions and cannot report; getBillingStatus is additionally called from server components (src/app/subscription/page.tsx:8, src/app/profile/page.tsx:11), so plan status has to travel as a prop to the client to be usable.

Acceptance criteria

  • Every event reports with the exact key and bounded values listed.
  • No id, file name, floor name, share key, email, address, coordinate or raw error string reaches Countly — verify on the wire, not just in the code.
  • Each reporter with real branch logic has a test that fails when the branch is broken.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Four of the five are in, merged to development via #721. New reporter src/lib/analytics/collabEvent.ts; account_password and sign_out extend authEvent.ts.

subscription_checkout is not included — this issue marks it later, and it was explicitly descoped for this pass.

Two gaps had to be closed before the funnel could say anything

  • forgotPasswordAction never bound its response. It awaited the fetch and returned a constant, so a rate limit was indistinguishable from a success. It now returns a rateLimited flag alongside the unchanged sent: true — no UI branch moves. Whether the Go endpoint actually 429s is not verifiable from this repo; resendVerificationAction already does the same check for its sibling endpoint, and if it never does the bucket sits at zero, which is itself the answer.
  • The reset-token validation had no catch at all. A transport failure left the screen on "Checking the reset link" forever with nothing reported. It now settles and reports check_failed.

The identity question, answered

This issue specified sign_out as the place to unbind the Countly identity. Nothing in this app binds one — set_id, change_id and user_details appear nowhere, and init() is given no device_id, so the SDK holds a self-generated anonymous id. There is nothing to unbind, so the event ships as a plain event. The reporter's doc records what to add when identity binding lands, including that the device-id reset must be queued after the event or the row is attributed to the incoming id instead of the outgoing one.

Reconnect storms

collab_join splits join from rejoin. The server emits project:joined on every reconnect and socket.io reconnects with backoff, so an unguarded report would read a flaky connection as dozens of people arriving. A per-socket flag makes the first a join; every later one is a rejoin carrying the drop reason, narrowed against socket.io's documented set with anything else collapsing to unknown. project:denied gets the same guard — a denied socket keeps retrying and is denied again each time.

Session duration is deliberately absent: a tab close never runs a clean disconnect, so any figure would be silently truncated.

Bug found on the way

The role select has no equality guard — Base UI's SelectItem calls onValueChange unconditionally — so re-picking the role a member already holds fired a live PATCH. It now returns early. A correctness win independent of the event, which would otherwise also have reported a change that changed nothing.

Other decisions

  • manage_collaborators folds email delivery into result rather than adding a boolean: "added but we could not email them" is something the owner has to act on, not a footnote on a success.
  • invalid_link appears under both link_opened and completed — a token that dies between the validate call and the submit is a different stuck user from one who opened an already-dead link.
  • sign_out keeps verify_pending separate from dashboard: the former routes to /register and is a "wrong email, start over" correction belonging next to the activation funnel, not a session ending.

Tests

src/lib/analytics/__tests__/collabEvent.test.ts — 15 cases: the password step/outcome pair and the two invalid_link moments, the sign-out surfaces, dropReason passing documented reasons through and collapsing everything else, the join/rejoin split and the denial, and the collaborator result and role handling — including one asserting the payload contains no @ at all.

issues.display_title: Issue #722: fix(map): dragging a shared corner splits the walls apart instead of welding them
issues.main_description_html:
Dragging a wall point that sits on a room corner in Map mode pulls one wall away and leaves its neighbour behind, opening a gap at the corner. The 2D editor welds the corner and moves both walls together; Map mode should match it.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Reported with two screenshots (samples/1.png, samples/2.png): before, a clean corner with a handle on it; after the drag, the two walls that met there have visibly separated.

Root cause

This is not a coding slip — it is a spec decision that turned out wrong in use, and it is currently locked in by a test.

The 2D editor welds coincident endpoints. On pointerdown, src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/interactions.ts:272 captures ctx.pending = joinGroup(ctx, h), and joinGroup (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/hittest.ts:11) is pointsAt(model, x, y, JOIN_EPS) — every editable endpoint within JOIN_EPS = 3 model units of the grabbed one (editor/constants.ts:5). The whole group then moves as one, which is why corners never come apart there. The helper's own comment says it outright: "Every endpoint coincident with (x,y) within eps — a shared corner that moves together."

Map mode moves exactly one point. moveWallVertex (src/lib/map/wall-vertex-edit.ts:194) matches on w.id !== wallId and then i === pointIndex. There is no coincidence search anywhere in the map path.

That was deliberate. PRD #681 §3 says "Move only the selected endpoint, not other endpoints with the same coordinate", and its non-goals list "no bulk shared-corner editing". The behaviour in the screenshots is the PRD being followed.

Scope

  1. moveWallVertex moves the weld group, not one point. Resolve the anchor point in the pre-drag canvas, then move every wall point within the same epsilon of it. Reuse JOIN_EPS from the engine's constants rather than a second magic number, so the two editors cannot drift apart.

    The group has to be resolved against the pre-drag snapshot, which the current call path already provides — Editor3DMapView recomputes from storedCanvasData on every pointermove, so the answer is stable for the whole gesture and no separate capture is needed.

  2. Curved walls join the group. Their endpoints are welded in 2D today, so excluding them here would leave exactly the reported gap whenever a curve meets the corner. Their bezier handles go stale, which is the same staleness 2D already ships; curve handles stay unexposed in Map mode, so this is not curve editing.

  3. Invert the two tests that pin the old behaviour, both in src/lib/map/__tests__/wall-vertex-edit.test.ts: "leaves a wall that ends on the same coordinate where it is (#681 §8)" at :89, and the same-reference assertion on walls[1] at :98. Add coverage for a point just outside the epsilon staying put.

  4. Record the reversal on #681 so the PRD text and the code stop disagreeing.

Out of scope

Deduplicating the handles. A welded corner still renders one dot per wall, stacked — visually a single dot, and dragging any of them now moves the same group, so there is nothing for a user to notice.

Acceptance criteria

  • Dragging a corner shared by two or more walls in Map mode moves every wall meeting there; the corner stays closed, as in samples/1.png.
  • A wall point outside the weld epsilon is unaffected.
  • One undo still restores the whole corner in a single step.
  • A curved wall sharing the corner moves with it.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Dragging a shared corner now moves every wall meeting there, as the 2D editor has always done.

The 2D drag captures joinGroup(ctx, h) on pointerdown — every editable endpoint within JOIN_EPS = 3 of the grabbed one — and moves the group as one. moveWallVertex now builds the same group from the same imported constant, so the two editors cannot drift apart.

The group resolves against the canvas the caller passes, which is held at its pre-drag state for the whole gesture, so a travelling point cannot pick up new neighbours. Walls away from the corner keep their object reference, and one undo still restores the whole corner in a step.

Curved walls join the group even though they get no handles of their own: their endpoints are welded in 2D too, and excluding them would reopen this gap whenever a curve meets the corner. A deliberate widening of this PRD's curve exclusion, recorded rather than slipped in.

The spec was the bug. #681 §3 asked for "move only the selected endpoint", its non-goals ruled out shared-corner editing, and a test asserted the split by name. Both tests that pinned it are inverted.

issues.display_title: Issue #724: fix(map): dragging a wall point re-anchors the projection, sliding and rescaling the whole floor
issues.main_description_html:
Dragging one wall point in Map mode slides the whole floor across the map and rescales it. Recorded in samples/test.mp4.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What the recording shows

Frame-by-frame against fixed basemap landmarks — the large pale polygon on the right, the road labels, the neighbouring buildings — the camera never moves. The floor does. Every corner shifts by roughly the same world-space vector while the map underneath stays put.

Root cause

computeCoordSpace (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:71) returns canvasData.coordSpace when the project has one, and otherwise derives the anchor from the geometry's bounding box — cxPx: (bbox.minX + bbox.maxX) / 2, with mpp from the box span. Every map projection in the app funnels through it.

moveWallVertex rewrites a wall point and preserves whatever fields the canvas already had. On a project without a stored coordSpace, moving a point changes the bounding box, which moves the anchor, which re-projects every wall on the floor. Measured on a 600×400 plan by pulling one corner to (900, −200):

before: cx=300 cy=200 mpp=0.0833
after:  cx=450 cy=100 mpp=0.0556

The anchor moved 150 px and the scale changed by a third — so the floor both slides and resizes against the real world. With a stored coordSpace the anchor holds and nothing drifts.

The 2D editor is unaffected because it has no map projection; that is why the same drag looks correct there.

This is not specific to vertex editing — any geometry edit on such a project re-anchors the floor — but vertex editing is the first feature that changes the bounding box interactively, so it is where it became visible.

Fix

Pin the anchor at the pre-drag geometry inside moveWallVertex, which is the single place both the live preview and the commit go through:

coordSpace: canvasData.coordSpace ?? computeCoordSpace(canvasData),

Computed from the canvas passed in, not the result — anchoring on the post-move geometry would still shift the floor on the very first drag. Stamping the value the floor is already being drawn at means nothing moves at the moment it is pinned; it only stops drifting afterwards.

This follows the convention the codebase already has for geometry writes: src/lib/editor/levels.ts:111 and src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts:286 both do base.coordSpace ?? computeCoordSpace(...) when adding a level.

Acceptance criteria

  • Dragging a wall point on a project with no stored coordSpace leaves every other wall where it was on the map.
  • The floor's size on the map is unchanged by the drag.
  • A project that already has a coordSpace keeps it untouched.
  • The anchor is taken from the geometry as it stood before the drag.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Two layers, because pinning coordSpace turned out to be only half of it.

The scale. computeCoordSpace falls back to the bounding-box centre, so on a project with no stored space a point move changed the anchor and mpp — measured at 150 px and a third of the scale on a 600×400 plan. moveWallVertex now pins it from the pre-drag geometry.

The pivots. All three placement frames pivot on a centre derived from live geometry — the project on its bbox (makePixelRotator), the building on its member levels' centres, the level on its own box. Pure translation is immune because the pivot cancels; rotation and scale are not. An untouched corner moved 93 px under a 30° level rotation, 36 px under a 1.2× scale, 84 px under a project rotation.

preserveMapPlacement compensates each frame's offset for its own pivot shift: for p → c + M(p − c) + off with M = R(θ)·s, holding the output fixed while c0 → c1 needs off1 = off0 + (I − M)(c0 − c1). Pivots are read from raw geometry, so the frames are independent and compose without ordering games.

This is the canvas-bounds intuition from the report, exactly. The 2D editor grows its page the same way — canvasBounds is the backdrop rect grown to cover anything drawn past it — and looks right because the grown bounds only frame the view. On the map the same growth is the pivot.

Every other geometry write has the same problem and is filed as #725 rather than half-fixed here.

issues.display_title: Issue #726: fix(map): dragging a wall corner leaves the floor slab behind
issues.main_description_html:
Dragging a wall corner in Map mode moves the walls but leaves the floor behind — the slab keeps the old shape and the walls sit off it.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

The map draws one floor slab per area polygon, not from the walls: canvasDataToGeoJson iterates level.layout.areas and extrudes each boundaries ring into a slab (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:889-909, with the open-to-below skip at :894 confirming these rings are the floor). buildingSolidsPx:997 does the same for the outdoor shell.

moveWallVertex rewrites layout.walls and nothing else, so the area rings stay where they were.

The area polygons are traced along wall centrelines — buildingSolidsPx's own comment says so — which is why a room corner sits exactly on the wall corner being dragged.

The 2D editor avoids this a different way: it re-derives rooms from the walls on every edit (recomputeRooms), so there is no stored polygon to fall out of step.

Fix

Extend the weld introduced in #722 to area boundaries: a boundary vertex within the same tolerance of the dragged corner moves with it.

Not by re-tracing the rooms. Detection would renumber the areas, and the Information records linked to them by id would come loose — a far worse outcome than a boundary that is approximate on an unusual drag. Moving the vertices keeps id, name, type and infoId intact.

Known and deliberately out of scope

Door and window openings drift the same way, and this is the next thing someone will report. They live in level.floorplanMeta.doors / .windows as absolute x1,y1,x2,y2 (geojson-utils.ts:812-813), so moving a wall leaves them floating. The 2D editor handles it with openingParamOnWall / placeOpeningOnWall (floorplan/editing.ts): it captures where the opening sits along its wall before the move — position t, its own length, and which way round it is stored — and re-places it after, keeping the door's real width and clamping it inside the wall.

That needs the same pair on the map model and is real work, not an extension of the weld. Filed separately when someone wants it.

Acceptance criteria

  • Dragging a room corner moves the floor slab with the walls; no gap opens between them.
  • Each area keeps its id, name, type and infoId.
  • An area nowhere near the dragged corner keeps its object reference.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

The floor now follows the walls.

The map draws one slab per area polygon, not from the walls, and those polygons are traced along wall centrelines — so a room corner sits exactly on the wall corner being dragged. The weld from #722 now covers area boundaries.

Not by re-tracing the rooms, which is how the 2D editor sidesteps this: it re-derives them on every edit and has no stored polygon to fall behind. Detection here would renumber the areas and the Information records linked by id would come loose. Moving the vertices keeps id, name, type and infoId, and an area away from the corner keeps its object reference.

Still open — door and window openings

They drift the same way. level.floorplanMeta.doors / .windows hold absolute coordinates, so a moved wall leaves them floating. The 2D editor handles it with openingParamOnWall / placeOpeningOnWall: capture where the opening sits along its wall — position, its own length, which way round it is stored — and re-place it after, keeping the door's real width and clamping it inside the wall. Porting that pair is real work rather than an extension of the weld, so it is left here for a decision rather than rushed in.
